sentences.en: What did exist were the old SGI documentation for the original STL.
sentences.zh: 当时存在的只有原始 STL 的旧版 SGI 文档。

sentences.en: And at some point we came across that and I didn't know what a reduction was at the time.
sentences.zh: 后来我们偶然发现了这些文档，但我当时根本不知道什么是归约（reduction）。

sentences.en: So anytime I would come across those documents about the SGI STL, I thought it was just gibberish.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我看到那些关于 SGI STL 的文档时，我都觉得那简直是天书。

sentences.en: I didn't know what they were talking about.
sentences.zh: 我根本看不懂他们在说什么。

sentences.en: I didn't know what an iterator was or a functor was, but I knew that std vector was helpful.
sentences.zh: 我不知道什么是迭代器，也不知道什么是函数对象，但我知道 std vector 很有用。

sentences.en: I just sort of assumed that this other stuff to the side was kind of for nerds or something.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是想当然地认为，旁边那些乱七八糟的东西大概是给书呆子看的。

sentences.en: But eventually I learned what std transform did and realized, oh, that's exactly what that's the kind of thing that we need to do this GPU parallelism stuff.
sentences.zh: 但后来我学会了 std transform 的用法，才意识到，哦，这正是我们做 GPU 并行计算所需要的东西。

sentences.en: And at that point, you know, I sort of had to get good with STL and figure all that stuff out.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我不得不开始深入学习 STL，并把所有这些东西搞清楚。

sentences.en: And it turns out that stuff is actually pretty useful and well designed, at least for the time.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那些东西确实非常有用且设计精良，至少在当时是这样。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 237, recorded on May 21st, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客，这是第 237 期，录制于 2025 年 5 月 21 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor and today with my co-host Bryce, we chat with Jared Hoborock, original author of the NVIDIA Thrust Parallel Algorithms Library.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，采访 NVIDIA Thrust 并行算法库的原创作者 Jared Hoberock。

sentences.en: This is part one of a most likely four or five part series.
sentences.zh: 这是这个系列节目的第一部分，大概会有四到五期。

sentences.en: Actual physical background is better than most folks' virtual background.
sentences.zh: 你真实的物理背景比大多数人的虚拟背景要好得多。

sentences.en: And you look like you're at like the edge of a national park with some – I don't actually know what your situation is, but it looks like a good situation.
sentences.zh: 看起来你就像是在国家公园的边缘——我其实不知道你具体在哪，但看起来环境很棒。

sentences.en: Like you've got windows behind your shelves and a window on the side.
sentences.zh: 就像你的书架后面有窗户，侧面也有窗户一样。

sentences.en: Walk us through – don't dox yourself if you don't want to, but when Bryce said that, I was also thinking, this is a setup that looks better than most CEOs in a keynote talk.
sentences.zh: 给我们介绍一下吧——如果你不想暴露隐私就不用说太细，但 Bryce 刚才那么一说，我也在想，这布置看起来比大多数 CEO 在主题演讲时的背景还要好。

sentences.en: Well, NVIDIA's salary goes a lot farther in Kansas City than it does in Silicon Valley, as it turns out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，NVIDIA 的薪水在堪萨斯城比在硅谷要经花得多。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Jared, do you live like out in the woods or like how rural is where you are?
sentences.zh: Jared，你住的地方是在树林里吗？或者说你住的地方有多偏远？

sentences.en: No, I live in a – I live in a suburb.
sentences.zh: 不，我住在一个郊区。

sentences.en: There's just, you know, a lot of greenery.
sentences.zh: 那里只是，你知道，有很多绿化。

sentences.en: So there's trees and – there's trees and lawns.
sentences.zh: 到处都是树和草坪。

sentences.en: Yeah, I do not have – I do not have greenery.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我这儿可没有绿化。

sentences.en: Do you have neighbors?
sentences.zh: 你有邻居吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I assume you definitely have neighbors, but it does look like you have a massive backyard or front yard, whatever that is in the background.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我假设你肯定有邻居，但背景里看起来你有一个巨大的后院或前院，不管那是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've got a neighbor.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有邻居。

sentences.en: Well, I've got lots of neighbors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有好多邻居。

sentences.en: I live in a little – actually, I live across the street from a Saturday Night Live cast member.
sentences.zh: 我住在一个小地方——其实我住的地方对面就住着一位《周六夜现场》的演员。

sentences.en: We live in a little cul-de-sac of mid-century modern architecture, and we've all got lawns and interesting-looking houses.
sentences.zh: 我们住在一个中世纪现代建筑风格的小死胡同里，大家都有草坪和外观很有趣的房子。

sentences.en: A man after my own heart.
sentences.zh: 真是志同道合的人。

sentences.en: I did not know this.
sentences.zh: 我之前都不知道这一点。

sentences.en: I'm a sucker for the mid-century modern architecture.
sentences.zh: 我特别迷恋中世纪现代建筑。

sentences.en: So we should talk to our boss about having our next research off-site in Kansas City then, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 听起来我们应该跟老板提议，下次研究团队的线下会议就定在堪萨斯城了。

sentences.en: We could have it downstairs.
sentences.zh: 我们可以就在楼下开会。

sentences.en: That is right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Potentially.
sentences.zh: 有可能。

sentences.en: You two have the same boss.
sentences.zh: 你们俩的老板是同一个人。

sentences.en: I forgot about that.
sentences.zh: 我把这茬给忘了。

sentences.en: That is – well, I guess I knew that, but I did not – I did not realize the possible podcast implications of that.
sentences.zh: 那是——好吧，我想我本来是知道的，但我没意识到这会对播客产生什么影响。

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, we should probably – now, I feel like some of this banter is going to make it onto the actual podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，我们大概应该——现在我觉得这些闲聊都要被录进播客里了。

sentences.en: Let's introduce our guest, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，还是先介绍一下我们的嘉宾吧。

sentences.en: We have the man, the myth, the developer behind the library that we spend an immense amount of time talking about on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们请到了这位传奇人物，也就是我们在播客中花费大量时间讨论的那个库的开发者。

sentences.en: The Thrust Parallel Algorithms Library, Jared Hobrock from Kansas City.
sentences.zh: Thrust 并行算法库的作者，来自堪萨斯城的 Jared Hoberock。

sentences.en: We spent a whole – we had our trip to Slovenia and to Italy where we were talking about Unique Count, an algorithm that I assume you personally authored back in the day,
sentences.zh: 我们之前去斯洛文尼亚和意大利旅行时，一直在讨论 Unique Count，我猜那是你当年亲自编写的算法，

sentences.en: only to realize that it was a reduction with some zip iterators behind the scene.
sentences.zh: 结果发现它其实就是一个带有 zip 迭代器的归约操作。

sentences.en: And, anyways, we're now talking to the individual that – I don't actually know where Thrust originated, if it was with your dissertation.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们现在正在和这位开发者对话——我其实不知道 Thrust 最初是怎么来的，是不是源于你的博士论文。

sentences.en: Anyways, we'll throw it over to you now, Jared.
sentences.zh: 总之，Jared，现在交给你了。

sentences.en: We'll get some updates from Bryce because he's in the States, not in New York.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会从 Bryce 那里得到一些更新，因为他在美国，不在纽约。

sentences.en: But before we do that –
sentences.zh: 但在那之前——

sentences.en: No, I am.
sentences.zh: 不，我在。

sentences.en: I'm home now.
sentences.zh: 我现在回家了。

sentences.en: Oh, are you home?
sentences.zh: 哦，你回家了吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, we'll get a little update from Bryce later.
sentences.zh: 那我们稍后再听 Bryce 的更新。

sentences.en: But we both work on the same research team and throw it back to wherever you want.
sentences.zh: 但我们都在同一个研究团队工作，你想从哪儿开始讲都行。

sentences.en: The first computer, the first time you encountered parallel programming, the first time you encountered a GPU,
sentences.zh: 第一台计算机，你第一次接触并行编程，第一次接触 GPU，

sentences.en: take it back however far you want and then bring us up to speed with where you are now, the Thrust Library.
sentences.zh: 你想追溯到多远都可以，然后带我们了解一下你现在的工作，也就是 Thrust 库。

sentences.en: You're working on, you know, things that are bigger and better, hopefully, than Thrust Library.
sentences.zh: 你现在正在做的事情，希望比 Thrust 库更宏大、更出色。

sentences.en: But, yeah, over to you.
sentences.zh: 总之，交给你了。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: Well, I'm always surprised to see that Thrust still gets talked about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看到 Thrust 至今仍被讨论，我总是感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: I'm surprised it could fill up enough content for, I don't know, some portion of your podcast so far.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶它竟然能为你们的播客提供这么多内容。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I guess just to talk a little bit about where it came from, it did originate as part of some work I was doing in grad school.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于它的起源，它确实是我在研究生期间所做工作的一部分。

sentences.en: So I came from a computer graphics background.
sentences.zh: 我有着计算机图形学的背景。

sentences.en: And in grad school, I was working on things like path tracing renderers on the GPU around the time that CUDA was first released.
sentences.zh: 在研究生期间，大约在 CUDA 刚发布的时候，我正在研究 GPU 上的路径追踪渲染器。

sentences.en: And Thrust sort of emerged from that renderer project because I needed something.
sentences.zh: Thrust 就是从那个渲染器项目中衍生出来的，因为我当时需要一些东西。

sentences.en: If you've ever written CUDA kernels, you know that there's a lot of, well, at the time, at least, not a lot of batteries were included with CUDA.
sentences.zh: 如果你写过 CUDA 内核，你就会知道，在当时，CUDA 并没有提供太多现成的工具。

sentences.en: So if you wanted to do anything with CUDA, it required a lot of effort, required a lot of labor.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想用 CUDA 做点什么，需要付出很大的努力和劳动。

sentences.en: And during that project while I was working on this renderer, I just noticed that I was, you know,
sentences.zh: 在那个项目期间，当我编写渲染器时，我注意到我一直在重复做某些内核启动所需的操作，

sentences.en: repeating certain things I needed to do for a kernel launch over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍地重复。

sentences.en: And then it became clear that, you know, we needed some more code reuse.
sentences.zh: 后来很明显，我们需要更多的代码复用。

sentences.en: And eventually this library sort of came together for automating some of the stuff you do as part of writing kernels and launching them.
sentences.zh: 最终，这个库就成型了，用于自动化编写和启动内核时的一些操作。

sentences.en: And that sort of evolved to become the Thrust library over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它逐渐演变成了 Thrust 库。

sentences.en: At some point, I learned about the standard template library and realized this is what we should be targeting.
sentences.zh: 在某个阶段，我了解到了标准模板库（STL），并意识到这才是我们应该瞄准的目标。

sentences.en: This is what we actually need.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们真正需要的东西。

sentences.en: And it sort of coalesced around this thing that already existed.
sentences.zh: 它最终围绕着这个已经存在的东西整合了起来。

sentences.en: So interesting.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: So you started off ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你最初是这样开始做 Thrust 的。

sentences.en: Thrust was not originally inspired by the STL.
sentences.zh: Thrust 最初并不是受 STL 启发的。

sentences.en: You started off as just a collection of, like, common utilities.
sentences.zh: 你最初只是把它当作一系列常用的工具集合。

sentences.en: And then you learned about the STL and then took inspiration from it.
sentences.zh: 然后你了解到了 STL，并从中汲取了灵感。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At some point, so this was probably back in 2007 or 8.
sentences.zh: 大概是在 2007 年或 2008 年的时候。

sentences.en: And things like cppreference.com didn't exist, right?
sentences.zh: 那时候像 cppreference.com 这样的网站还没出现，对吧？

sentences.en: Stack overflow maybe didn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: Stack Overflow 可能也还没出现。

sentences.en: But what did exist were the old SGI documentation for the original STL.
sentences.zh: 但当时存在的只有原始 STL 的旧版 SGI 文档。

sentences.en: And at some point, we came across that.
sentences.zh: 后来我们偶然发现了这些文档。

sentences.en: And I didn't know what a reduction was at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时根本不知道什么是归约。

sentences.en: So anytime I would come across those documents about the SGI STL, I thought it was just, you know, gibberish.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我看到那些关于 SGI STL 的文档时，我都觉得那简直是天书。

sentences.en: I didn't know what they were talking about.
sentences.zh: 我根本看不懂他们在说什么。

sentences.en: I didn't know what an iterator was or a functor was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道什么是迭代器，也不知道什么是函数对象。

sentences.en: But I knew that, like, std vector was helpful.
sentences.zh: 但我知道 std vector 很有用。

sentences.en: And I just sort of assumed that this other stuff to the side was kind of for nerds or something.
sentences.zh: 我只是想当然地认为，旁边那些乱七八糟的东西大概是给书呆子看的。

sentences.en: But eventually, I learned what std transform did and realized, oh, that's exactly what – that's the kind of thing that we need to do this GPU parallelism stuff.
sentences.zh: 但后来我学会了 std transform 的用法，才意识到，哦，这正是我们做 GPU 并行计算所需要的东西。

sentences.en: And at that point, you know, I sort of had to get good with STL and figure all that stuff out.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我不得不开始深入学习 STL，并把所有这些东西搞清楚。

sentences.en: And it turns out that stuff is actually pretty useful and well-designed, at least for the time.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，那些东西确实非常有用且设计精良，至少在当时是这样。

sentences.en: But maybe originally wasn't presented in the most sort of – it wasn't obvious why it might be useful at the time because C++ in, like, 2008-ish,
sentences.zh: 但最初的呈现方式可能并不是最直观的——在 2008 年左右，人们并不清楚它为什么有用，因为当时的 C++ 并不处于一种能高效使用 STL 的状态，对吧？

sentences.en: it wasn't really in a state where you could use the STL in a productive way, right?
sentences.zh: 那是在 lambda 表达式出现之前。

sentences.en: That would be before things like lambdas.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切对我来说看起来非常陌生，直到后来我弄明白了它的用途。

sentences.en: And so it all looked very alien to me until eventually sort of figured out what the purpose was.
sentences.zh: 而 GPU 并行计算的使用场景让我豁然开朗。

sentences.en: And having the use case in GPU parallelism was sort of what made that click for me.
sentences.zh: 你所做的这些最终导致 Thrust 诞生的工作，是在 CUDA 之前吗？

sentences.en: Did this work that you're doing on – that eventually led to Thrust, was that – was any of that pre-CUDA?
sentences.zh: 还是说都是在 CUDA 首次发布之后？

sentences.en: Or was it all, like, after the initial CUDA release?
sentences.zh: 在 CUDA 出来之前，我们写的是所谓的 GPGPU，对吧？

sentences.en: Before CUDA came out, we would write – they had what was called GPGPU, right?
sentences.zh: 也就是在 GPU 上进行通用编程。

sentences.en: So general-purpose programming on GPUs.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，这意味着你要用 HLSL 或当时 OpenGL 的着色器语言来编写着色器。

sentences.en: And in those days, that meant you were writing shaders in something like HLSL or whatever the OpenGL shading language was at the time.
sentences.zh: 你实际上是在尝试用像素着色器来实现你想要的功能。

sentences.en: You were sort of trying to do what you wanted to do in a graphic – in, like, in a pixel shader, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以当时确实有这方面的工作。

sentences.en: So there was a bit of that going on.
sentences.zh: 但我们真正想要的是——渲染器周围的代码全是 C++，你更希望全部用 C++ 编写，而不必在 C++ 渲染器代码和某种伪 C++ 语言的着色器代码之间来回切换。

sentences.en: But we really wanted – like, the surrounding code in a renderer was all C++, and you just prefer to write it all in C++ and not have to switch between, you know,
sentences.zh: 总之，在 CUDA 出来之前，我们只能将就着那样做。

sentences.en: the renderer code in C++ and then the shader code in some sort of pseudo C++-like language.
sentences.zh: 但一旦 CUDA 发布，且 C++ 在当时勉强能用，那可比在图形着色器里折腾要好得多。

sentences.en: And anyway, before CUDA came out, that's sort of what we had to settle for.
sentences.zh: 所以后来我开始基于 CUDA 开发 GPU 光线追踪器。

sentences.en: But once CUDA did come out and C++ sort of – kind of, sort of worked at the time, that was just, like, so much better than trying to do things in shaders, in graphic shaders.
sentences.zh: 当然，渲染器是一个 C++ 应用程序，而 CUDA 在当时已经非常接近 C++ 了。

sentences.en: So at some point, I started working on a GPU ray tracer based on CUDA.
sentences.zh: 总之，当 CUDA C++ 真正可用时，Thrust 就是从那项工作中演变而来的。

sentences.en: And, of course, that would be – like, the renderer was a C++ application, and the CUDA stuff was close enough to C++ at the time.
sentences.zh: 在 CUDA 之前，戴维斯大学的一些人曾用图形着色器做过类似 Thrust 的东西。

sentences.en: So anyway, at some point, Thrust sort of evolved from that work when CUDA C++ actually did become available.
sentences.zh: 他们有着同样的想法。

sentences.en: Before CUDA, there was – some people at Davis had sort of a Thrust-like thing they were doing with graphic shaders.
sentences.zh: 你拥有这些并行原语，但他们是将它们编译成图形着色器。

sentences.en: They sort of had the same idea.
sentences.zh: 当然，那只是一个研究项目。

sentences.en: You had these parallel primitives, but they were sort of compiling them to graphic shaders.
sentences.zh: 没有人用它来开发产品之类的。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, it was just a research project.
sentences.zh: 但这个想法其实已经存在很久了。

sentences.en: No one was building products with it or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我想即使是 Ian Buck 在斯坦福的工作，也是针对着色器的，当时可能也有类似的味道。

sentences.en: But the idea has sort of been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 但这都是很久以前的事了，在 CUDA 诞生之前。

sentences.en: I think even Ian Buck's sort of work at Stanford was – it was also targeting shaders and maybe had some of the same kind of flavor at the time.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说在发现 STL 之前，你并没有考虑过归约。

sentences.en: But this is all, like, a long time ago, you know, before CUDA, you know, ever existed.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，Thrust-reduce 是 Thrust 库中最重要的算法之一。

sentences.en: So you said at one point that pre-discovering STL, you weren't really thinking about reduces.
sentences.zh: 归约是并行计算的核心。

sentences.en: And you can correct me if I'm wrong, but, like, you know, the Thrust-reduce is, you know, a – I don't know what you call it, a paramount algorithm of the Thrust library.
sentences.zh: 我知道 Jeff Dean 的 MapReduce 是在 2003 或 2004 年发布的。

sentences.en: Like, reductions are the bread and butter of parallel compute.
sentences.zh: 所以当你处理这些重复的 CUDA 内核模式并致力于开发这个算法库，然后发现了 STL 时——我是说，这可是 Bryce 和我最喜欢的算法之一。

sentences.en: And I know that – I think it was 2003 or 2004 that the Jeff Dean MapReduce came out.
sentences.zh: 你当时了解归约和并行归约吗？

sentences.en: So when you're working on these repetitive CUDA kernel patterns and you're working towards this algorithm library and then you discover the STL – I mean, it's both, you know,
sentences.zh: 当时的学术文献是什么情况？

sentences.en: Bryce and my – one of our favorite algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 因为听起来像是你偶然发现了 STL，然后它帮你理清了思路。

sentences.en: What is – were you aware of, like, reductions and parallel reductions at that point?
sentences.zh: 那是导致 std-reduce（或者说 thrust-reduce）诞生的原因吗？

sentences.en: Like, what's the state of the academic literature?
sentences.zh: 还是说它在那之前就已经明确存在于你的算法库中了，只是刚好匹配上了？

sentences.en: Because you made it sound like you stumbled upon the STL and that helped you crystallize it.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: Like, was that what led to, like, std-reduce – or not std-reduce, but, like, thrust-reduce?
sentences.zh: 记住，这是在路径追踪渲染器的背景下。

sentences.en: Or was that, like, clearly a part of your algorithm library before then and it just kind of matched up well?
sentences.zh: 我需要发射一堆光线，对于每条光线，追踪它。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 根本不需要归约。

sentences.en: So this – remember, this is in the context of a path-tracing renderer.
sentences.zh: 我当时确实不知道什么是归约。

sentences.en: So I needed to fire a bunch of rays, you know, for each ray, trace a ray.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道——

sentences.en: There was no need for a reduction.
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I certainly didn't know what a reduction was at the time.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我是 2008 年到 2014 年上学的。

sentences.en: I wasn't aware that –
sentences.zh: 也许我没学过，但我在学习编程语言时，函数式编程已经很流行了。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 所以归约和折叠（fold）到处都是。

sentences.en: And that's – like, to me, like, I went to school 2008 to 2014.
sentences.zh: 你去学一门语言，它们都有这种算法。

sentences.en: Maybe didn't learn about it, but, like, functional programming was a thing while I was learning programming languages.
sentences.zh: 但在你那个时代，你说你甚至都不知道——那不是一个——

sentences.en: So, like, reductions and folds, it's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 记住，当时它并没有到处都是。

sentences.en: Like, you go to a language, they've got an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 是我们把这个术语引入 C++ 的，所以它当时并不在那门语言里。

sentences.en: But at your time, you're saying you weren't even aware – that wasn't like a –
sentences.zh: 我在研究生院上过一门编程语言课，是用 OCaml 教的，那是一门函数式语言。

sentences.en: Well, remember, it wasn't everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但我当时根本没听懂。

sentences.en: We introduced the term into C++, so it wasn't in that language.
sentences.zh: 我们把这个术语引入 C++ 的，所以它当时并不在那门语言里。

sentences.en: I took one – I took a programming languages class in grad school, and that class was taught in OCaml, which is a functional language.
sentences.zh: 我在研究生院上过一门编程语言课，是用 OCaml 教的，那是一门函数式语言。

sentences.en: And I didn't understand it.
sentences.zh: 但我当时根本没听懂。

sentences.en: I didn't just – I didn't get it.
sentences.zh: 我当时不仅仅是——我没弄明白。

sentences.en: It didn't click for me at the time.
sentences.zh: 那时候我没能领会其中的精髓。

sentences.en: Now I sort of get – I understand functional programming a lot better.
sentences.zh: 现在我算是弄懂了——我对函数式编程的理解深刻多了。

sentences.en: But at the time, I didn't – I tried to write everything as if I was writing C code, and it just never really clicked for me.
sentences.zh: 但当时我没有——我试图用写 C 代码的方式去写所有东西，所以一直没真正领悟。

sentences.en: And certainly wasn't exposed to something like a fold until much later in my career.
sentences.zh: 而且直到职业生涯很晚的时候，我才接触到像 fold（折叠）这样的概念。

sentences.en: So, no, at the time when Thrust was coming together, you know, I probably didn't learn about a reduction until someone demonstrated how to –
sentences.zh: 所以，不，在 Thrust 刚成型的时候，你知道，我可能直到有人演示了如何——

sentences.en: probably until Mark Harris demonstrated how to do it in CUDA.
sentences.zh: 可能直到 Mark Harris 演示了如何在 CUDA 中实现它，我才学会 reduction（归约）。

sentences.en: That is – that's both surprising and inspiring, that the fact that it's such an essential part of Thrust and CUDA programming in general,
sentences.zh: 这既令人惊讶又令人振奋，毕竟它是 Thrust 和整个 CUDA 编程中如此核心的一部分，

sentences.en: that you didn't discover that until so late.
sentences.zh: 而你竟然直到那么晚才发现它。

sentences.en: I would have just assumed it was, like, part of the genesis of ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我本来还以为它是 Thrust 诞生之初就有的呢。

sentences.en: Well, parallel programming at the time was something that people did at National Labs, and they did it on Intel chips.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时的并行编程是国家实验室的人在做的事，而且他们是在 Intel 芯片上做的。

sentences.en: And they – I imagine everything they did was sort of ad hoc.
sentences.zh: 而且他们——我想他们所做的一切都比较临时凑合。

sentences.en: It's not like there were libraries of, you know, parallel primitives in 2005 or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 2005 年的时候，可不像现在这样有各种并行原语库。

sentences.en: But maybe the closest thing there was was threading building blocks.
sentences.zh: 当时最接近的可能就是 Threading Building Blocks（TBB）了。

sentences.en: I don't know when that came out, but they – TBB probably had a reduce at the time, but I had never used TBB.
sentences.zh: 我不记得它是什么时候出来的，但它们——TBB 当时可能确实有 reduce 操作，但我从没用过 TBB。

sentences.en: It's not something I was experienced in.
sentences.zh: 那不是我擅长的领域。

sentences.en: I was – I was just – like I said, my background was in GPGPU, and that meant doing stuff with pixel shaders.
sentences.zh: 我当时——我只是——就像我说的，我的背景是 GPGPU，这意味着是用像素着色器（pixel shaders）来做东西。

sentences.en: You couldn't do a reduction in a pixel shader at the time.
sentences.zh: 那时候你没法在像素着色器里做归约。

sentences.en: It wasn't possible.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: So, no communication was possible, actually, in pixel shaders at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，实际上当时在像素着色器中无法进行通信。

sentences.en: So, I do believe that, like, the original origin of the term reduce comes from, like, APL and Ken Iverson.
sentences.zh: 所以，我确实相信 reduce 这个术语的最初起源来自 APL 和 Ken Iverson。

sentences.en: And then the question is, when did it become a popular thing in parallel programming?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，它是什么时候在并行编程中流行起来的呢？

sentences.en: So, I can think of a couple different places.
sentences.zh: 我想到了几个不同的地方。

sentences.en: First of all, MPI, the message-passing interface, which was created in the 90s, has a reduction primitive.
sentences.zh: 首先是 MPI，即消息传递接口，它创建于 90 年代，拥有归约原语。

sentences.en: And I think that's certainly one of the places where the notion of a generalized, semi-generalized reduction would have come up as a basic parallel operation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这无疑是广义或半广义归约概念作为基本并行操作出现的地方之一。

sentences.en: TBB certainly came later, but I do wonder – I asked ChatGPT in the background, so it's looking for answers.
sentences.zh: TBB 肯定是在那之后出现的，但我确实很好奇——我在后台问了 ChatGPT，它正在找答案。

sentences.en: But I do wonder, where is the first programming language that had a parallel reduction operation, a generalized parallel reduction operation?
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，第一个拥有并行归约操作，即广义并行归约操作的编程语言是哪一个？

sentences.en: And by generalized, I mean one where you could plug in different operators.
sentences.zh: 所谓广义，我是指那种可以插入不同运算符的归约。

sentences.en: I wonder which the first would have been.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇哪一个是第一个。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我完全不知道。

sentences.en: I'm – I assume the term reduce comes from –
sentences.zh: 我——我假设 reduce 这个词来自——

sentences.en: It actually – it comes from APL.
sentences.zh: 它实际上——它来自 APL。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, so APL, the book was written in 1962.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，APL 的书是 1962 年写的。

sentences.en: The first implementation was 1966.
sentences.zh: 第一个实现是在 1966 年。

sentences.en: But the term reduce comes from these array languages where when you perform a reduction on a matrix, you are reducing the dimensions by one.
sentences.zh: 但 reduce 这个词来自这些数组语言，当你对矩阵执行归约时，你是在将维度减少一。

sentences.en: So if – if on a matrix, if you do a column-wise or a row-wise reduction, you end up with a rank one array.
sentences.zh: 所以如果在矩阵上进行列向或行向归约，最终会得到一个秩为 1 的数组。

sentences.en: If you are doing a reduction on a rank one array, you end up with a rank zero scalar.
sentences.zh: 如果你对秩为 1 的数组进行归约，最终会得到一个秩为 0 的标量。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people think that the term reduce comes from that you're reducing a bunch of elements down to a single element, but that's actually not it.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人认为 reduce 这个词是因为你把一堆元素减少到了一个元素，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The term comes from – you are reducing the dimensions on an arbitrarily ranked array from N to N minus one.
sentences.zh: 这个词的由来是——你正在将任意秩数组的维度从 N 减少到 N 减 1。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: And to think that it comes from a sequence down to a scalar, I mean, it's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 认为它来自序列到标量的归约，我的意思是，这也不算错。

sentences.en: It is technically a subset of the arbitrarily ranked array of N rank to N minus one rank.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，它确实是 N 秩到 N-1 秩的任意秩数组的一个子集。

sentences.en: But, I mean, this is all very fascinating because, I mean, the state of Thrust today is a very polished, usable, parallel algorithm library, which, as you mentioned earlier,
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，这一切都非常迷人，因为 Thrust 的现状是一个非常完善、可用且强大的并行算法库，正如你之前提到的，

sentences.en: like you said, you're surprised that people are still squeezing so much usefulness out of it.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，你很惊讶人们仍然能从中榨取出这么多价值。

sentences.en: But, like, I think of Thrust Transform Reduce and Thrust Reduce and Thrust Inclusive and Exclusive Scan as, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为 Thrust 的 Transform Reduce、Thrust Reduce 以及 Inclusive 和 Exclusive Scan 就像是，

sentences.en: very fundamental primitives that if I were to write the history for this algorithm library, like, of course, that is what you started with.
sentences.zh: 非常基础的原语，如果我要为这个算法库写历史，那当然，这就是你起步的地方。

sentences.en: But you're saying that that wasn't the case at all.
sentences.zh: 但你却说根本不是这样。

sentences.en: Like, you were working on ray tracing and these things evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 就像你当时在做光线追踪，这些东西是随着时间推移演变而来的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and especially for something like Transform Reduce, that sort of, you know, that evolved as a means to get fusion between, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是对于 Transform Reduce 这样的东西，它演变出来是为了实现融合，你知道，

sentences.en: something like a Transform and a Reduction because, you know,
sentences.zh: 像 Transform 和 Reduction 之间的融合，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: you want to avoid the memory traffic that would occur if you applied those as two separate passes rather than one fused pass together.
sentences.zh: 你想要避免如果将它们作为两个独立步骤而不是一个融合步骤执行时所产生的内存流量。

sentences.en: And it wasn't obvious, at least to us, that that's something that could be really useful to do.
sentences.zh: 而且至少对我们来说，这是否真的有用并不是显而易见的。

sentences.en: But now, like you said, maybe it's one of the first things that you would reach for whenever you need to do something interesting.
sentences.zh: 但现在，就像你说的，这可能是你每当需要做点有趣的事情时，首先会想到的东西之一。

sentences.en: When, Jared, when did the notion of the fancy iterators, of the lazy iterators come in?
sentences.zh: Jared，花式迭代器（fancy iterators）和惰性迭代器（lazy iterators）的概念是什么时候引入的？

sentences.en: Like, or let me put it another way.
sentences.zh: 或者换种说法。

sentences.en: At what point did you realize that instead of having a special Transform Reduce op, that you could have a Reduce op and something like a Transform iterator?
sentences.zh: 你在什么时候意识到，与其拥有一个专门的 Transform Reduce 操作，不如拥有一个 Reduce 操作和一个类似 Transform 迭代器的东西？

sentences.en: Well, originally, I think, so, at some point, collaborator Nathan Bell came on to work on the project.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初，我想，在某个时候，合作者 Nathan Bell 加入了项目。

sentences.en: And it was sort of the two of us working.
sentences.zh: 当时基本上是我们俩在工作。

sentences.en: And before we had settled on the idea that the SGI STL API was something that we needed to target, there was some, like,
sentences.zh: 在我们确定 SGI STL API 是我们需要瞄准的目标之前，有一些，比如，

sentences.en: it wasn't clear what the inputs to the algorithm should even be, right?
sentences.zh: 甚至不清楚算法的输入应该是什么，对吧？

sentences.en: So it wasn't even clear that iterators were the sort of model to target.
sentences.zh: 所以甚至不清楚迭代器是否是应该瞄准的模型。

sentences.en: And Nathan had a background in Python.
sentences.zh: 而且 Nathan 有 Python 背景。

sentences.en: So he was used to, like, NumPy.
sentences.zh: 所以他习惯了像 NumPy 那样的东西。

sentences.en: And he had suggested, I remember he had suggested, well, what if the inputs to these algorithms were more like generators?
sentences.zh: 我记得他建议过，如果这些算法的输入更像生成器会怎样？

sentences.en: So they're sort of just, like, black box functions that you call and they give, you know, they return something to you.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是你调用的黑盒函数，它们会返回一些东西给你。

sentences.en: So, and at some point, it was clear that, like, that was not going to work.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时候，很明显那行不通。

sentences.en: Like, C++ wasn't, like, Python.
sentences.zh: C++ 不像 Python。

sentences.en: And that couldn't be made to work correctly.
sentences.zh: 那没法正确实现。

sentences.en: So iterators was probably something that we needed to understand really well and target.
sentences.zh: 所以迭代器可能是我们需要深入理解并瞄准的东西。

sentences.en: And at that point, I realized I needed to, like, get better at C++ because, like, the stuff going on in the Boost iterator library was pretty wild at the time.
sentences.zh: 在那时，我意识到我需要提高我的 C++ 水平，因为当时 Boost 迭代器库里的东西简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So, you know, I started mining booster ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我开始挖掘 Boost 的想法。

sentences.en: And, you know, they've got the iterator library.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们有迭代器库。

sentences.en: And that's, I mean, Thrust essentially cargo-culted all that stuff and brought it all in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，Thrust 本质上是“崇拜式”地照搬了所有那些东西并将其整合进来。

sentences.en: I don't remember exactly.
sentences.zh: 我不记得确切的时间了。

sentences.en: I'm sure the release notes say exactly when this came in.
sentences.zh: 我相信发布说明里肯定写了这是什么时候加入的。

sentences.en: But at some point,
sentences.zh: 但在某个时候，

sentences.en: it became clear that adopting that sort of model would be a good idea because it would allow things like Fusion and transform-reduce and zip and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 很明显采用那种模型是个好主意，因为它能实现像融合（Fusion）、transform-reduce 和 zip 等等这类功能。

sentences.en: Did transform-iterator come before transform-reduce or did it come after?
sentences.zh: Transform-iterator 是在 transform-reduce 之前还是之后出现的？

sentences.en: Or do you recall?
sentences.zh: 或者你还记得吗？

sentences.en: I don't remember.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: I believe from – because I – so a little piece of context here is that I had the unfortunate distinction of having to do a significant amount of version control engineering on Thrust because we had to – we've had to migrate it between three different version control systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我相信从——因为我——这里提供一点背景，我有幸承担了在 Thrust 上进行大量版本控制工程的艰巨任务，因为我们不得不——我们不得不将它在三个不同的版本控制系统之间迁移。

sentences.en: And so I've looked through all the commits, at least all the commit messages, a couple times.
sentences.zh: 所以我把所有的提交，至少是所有的提交信息，都看过好几遍了。

sentences.en: And I believe, if I recall correctly,
sentences.zh: 我相信，如果我没记错的话，

sentences.en: that transform-reduce came first and that later transform – like the current implementation where transform-reduce is implemented as just reduce with transform-iterators came later.
sentences.zh: transform-reduce 是先出现的，而后来——比如当前的实现，即 transform-reduce 仅仅作为带有 transform-iterator 的 reduce 来实现——是后来才有的。

sentences.en: Just in general, like right now at this point in its life cycle, you know, Thrust is mature and it's sort of implemented in terms of itself, right?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，就像现在这个生命周期的阶段，你知道，Thrust 已经成熟了，它基本上是基于自身实现的，对吧？

sentences.en: So like one algorithm can implement itself by lowering onto another.
sentences.zh: 所以一个算法可以通过调用另一个算法来实现自己。

sentences.en: But, you know, projects don't begin like that, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，项目开始时并不是这样的，对吧？

sentences.en: They begin as like you put in this hack into this part of the code to make it work.
sentences.zh: 它们开始时就像是你往代码的某一部分塞进一个 hack 来让它工作。

sentences.en: But, you know, you really – you sort of know that it should sort of just use itself in a different way and be sort of self-similar.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你确实——你多少知道它应该以不同的方式使用自身，并具有某种自相似性。

sentences.en: But – so it doesn't surprise me that maybe transform-reduce or transform came before transform-iterator.
sentences.zh: 但是——所以 transform-reduce 或 transform 在 transform-iterator 之前出现，我并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So Thrust has – I think its architecture is in some ways elegant.
sentences.zh: 所以 Thrust 有——我认为它的架构在某些方面很优雅。

sentences.en: In some ways there's some dark holes of it.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面也有一些黑暗的角落。

sentences.en: But I think by far the most beautiful part of Thrust is the – what's called like the generic backend, the dispatch layer.
sentences.zh: 但我认为 Thrust 最美妙的部分绝对是——所谓的通用后端，即分发层（dispatch layer）。

sentences.en: So when you write a Thrust backend, you can customize how each function in that backend.
sentences.zh: 所以当你编写一个 Thrust 后端时，你可以自定义该后端中的每个函数。

sentences.en: You can customize how reduce works, how transform works, how sort works, how unique works.
sentences.zh: 你可以自定义 reduce 如何工作，transform 如何工作，sort 如何工作，unique 如何工作。

sentences.en: But there's this generic layer where at minimum your backend has to customize like five or six basis algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 但有一个通用层，你的后端至少需要自定义五六个基础算法。

sentences.en: And you can customize more if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，也可以自定义更多。

sentences.en: But if you don't customize more, then all the rest of the algorithms are implemented in terms of those five or six basis algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不自定义更多，那么其余所有的算法都是基于那五六个基础算法实现的。

sentences.en: And those implementations in terms of the basis algorithms are in this generic layer.
sentences.zh: 而那些基于基础算法的实现就在这个通用层中。

sentences.en: And I think that's the most beautiful part of ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是 Thrust 最美妙的部分。

sentences.en: And actually if you're – like it's one of the best places to like find examples of how to write good Thrust code.
sentences.zh: 实际上，如果你是——这确实是寻找如何编写优秀 Thrust 代码示例的最佳地方之一。

sentences.en: Because like that's where you can go to find like the unique count implementation that we've talked about on the podcast before in terms of reduce.
sentences.zh: 因为那就是你可以找到我们之前在播客中讨论过的基于 reduce 的 unique count 实现的地方。

sentences.en: Or like the reduce implementation in terms of like transform iterators.
sentences.zh: 或者像基于 transform-iterator 的 reduce 实现。

sentences.en: It's a really – it's a very elegant part of the code.
sentences.zh: 这是代码中非常优雅的一部分。

sentences.en: I have to disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不得不表示反对。

sentences.en: I think it's a gigantic mess of spaghetti code.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一团巨大的意大利面条式代码。

sentences.en: So I know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: Like the idea is you want to call an algorithm and maybe get a default implementation if there's not a specialization and a backend somewhere.
sentences.zh: 比如这个想法是，你想要调用一个算法，如果某处没有特化和后端，就得到一个默认实现。

sentences.en: I think we have better ways to do that in C++ in 2025.
sentences.zh: 我认为在 2025 年的 C++ 中我们有更好的方法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: But at the time, I remember – at the time, we didn't – there wasn't a good understanding of things like customization point objects and how to make that stuff work.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，我记得——在当时，我们没有——对定制点对象（customization point objects）以及如何让这些东西工作没有很好的理解。

sentences.en: So the way it does work to the extent that it does work was sort of implemented in what C++03 made possible because that was sort of the constraints of the time.
sentences.zh: 所以它能工作到这种程度，是因为它是用 C++03 所能实现的方式编写的，因为那是当时的限制。

sentences.en: But what you get is this mess – I know it's a gigantic mess of spaghetti.
sentences.zh: 但你得到的是这团乱麻——我知道这是一团巨大的意大利面条。

sentences.en: But it does work.
sentences.zh: 但它确实能工作。

sentences.en: It is sometimes very subtle because it works on the principle of ADL dispatch.
sentences.zh: 它有时非常微妙，因为它基于 ADL 分发原则。

sentences.en: And there's some amount of upcasting of execution policies.
sentences.zh: 而且涉及一定程度的执行策略向上转型（upcasting）。

sentences.en: So there's this tag, the execution policy.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个标签，即执行策略。

sentences.en: And that is used to route your call to the right place.
sentences.zh: 它被用来将你的调用路由到正确的地方。

sentences.en: And as it goes through all of these forwarding layers,
sentences.zh: 当它穿过所有这些转发层时，

sentences.en: the forwarding layers have to ensure that the execution policy is correctly casted or upcasted to the most derived execution policy so that it dispatches to the right place.
sentences.zh: 转发层必须确保执行策略被正确地转换或向上转型为最派生的执行策略，以便它能分发到正确的地方。

sentences.en: And if any of that goes wrong, you end up with all sorts of fun.
sentences.zh: 如果其中任何一步出错，你就会遇到各种各样的麻烦。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't have to do that anymore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你现在不需要那样做了。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of the reasons that it does work like that is because there were no forwarding references at the time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它之所以那样工作，很大程度上是因为当时没有转发引用（forwarding references）。

sentences.en: Yeah, you could do much better these days, I think, if someone was so inclined.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想如果有人愿意的话，现在可以做得好得多。

sentences.en: So it's very interesting to me to hear that Nathan Bell, who was one of the other founders of Thrust, was a Python person when he was a NumPy person.
sentences.zh: 所以听到 Nathan Bell（Thrust 的另一位创始人）曾经是 NumPy 的 Python 用户，这对我来说非常有趣。

sentences.en: Because, Jared, do you know the largest user by volume and compute of Thrust today?
sentences.zh: 因为，Jared，你知道今天 Thrust 按容量和计算量最大的用户是谁吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: So I think I can give you a pretty accurate accounting of the top users of Thrust, specifically ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我可以给你一个关于 Thrust（特别是 Thrust）顶级用户的相当准确的统计。

sentences.en: I'm going to exclude libraries that use a lot of Cub and some ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我将排除那些大量使用 Cub 和部分 Thrust 的库。

sentences.en: I mean, just people that will heavily rely on ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅是那些严重依赖 Thrust 的人。

sentences.en: And by users, the metric I'm measuring by is not lines of code written or number of developers using it,
sentences.zh: 按用户来说，我衡量的指标不是编写的代码行数或使用它的开发人员数量，

sentences.en: but I mean number of GPUs right this moment that are running that Thrust code.
sentences.zh: 而是指此时此刻正在运行该 Thrust 代码的 GPU 数量。

sentences.en: And I'm not sure which of these two is number one and number two, but I think number one is Coupie.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这两个谁是第一谁是第二，但我认为第一是 CuPy。

sentences.en: And Coupie is just a CUDA-accelerated version of NumPy.
sentences.zh: CuPy 只是 NumPy 的 CUDA 加速版本。

sentences.en: So I think there's something very elegant here that back in the day, Jared and this NumPy fellow came and wrote Thrust, and Thrust has some of that NumPy DNA in it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这里有一些非常优雅的地方，当年 Jared 和这位 NumPy 的伙伴一起来写了 Thrust，而 Thrust 拥有一些 NumPy 的基因。

sentences.en: And then, like, 15 years later, Thrust is the thing that powers Coupie, the GPU-accelerated NumPy.
sentences.zh: 然后，15 年后，Thrust 成为了驱动 CuPy（GPU 加速的 NumPy）的东西。

sentences.en: Now, you asked the other ones, the one that I think is probably number two, and again, this is by the metric I gave of, like, number of, like,
sentences.zh: 现在，你问了其他的，我认为可能是第二名的，同样，这是根据我给出的指标，即，

sentences.en: amount of Thrust code that's running right now would be PyTorch.
sentences.zh: 目前正在运行的 Thrust 代码量，那应该是 PyTorch。

sentences.en: And PyTorch is in more use than Coupie, but PyTorch uses Thrust in fewer places than Coupie does.
sentences.zh: PyTorch 的使用量比 CuPy 大，但 PyTorch 在比 CuPy 更少的地方使用 Thrust。

sentences.en: Coupie uses Thrust very, very extensively to implement a ton of the different algorithMs.
sentences.zh: CuPy 非常非常广泛地使用 Thrust 来实现大量的不同算法。

sentences.en: It always uses Cub, but it uses it pretty extensively.
sentences.zh: 它总是使用 Cub，但它使用 Thrust 也相当广泛。

sentences.en: At least that's my understanding.
sentences.zh: 至少我是这么理解的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I would say Coupie, PyTorch are the top two.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我会说 CuPy 和 PyTorch 是前两名。

sentences.en: Rapids is probably, like, number three or number four.
sentences.zh: Rapids 可能是第三或第四名。

sentences.en: And then I think after that, I think it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我想很难说。

sentences.en: There's probably one or two more Python users, and then probably it's whoever the largest C++ user is.
sentences.zh: 可能还有一两个 Python 用户，然后可能就是最大的 C++ 用户了。

sentences.en: But, like, definitely the top three or four users of the Thrust library today are Python frameworks.
sentences.zh: 但是，今天 Thrust 库的前三或前四名用户绝对是 Python 框架。

sentences.en: That's interesting because around 2009, there was sort of a question of what's next.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为在 2009 年左右，有一个关于下一步该做什么的问题。

sentences.en: There was a question, like, what was going to be next for Thrust?
sentences.zh: 有一个问题，比如，Thrust 的下一步是什么？

sentences.en: And we had abandoned plans for doing a bunch of, like, numeric extensions, some very NumPy-like numeric extensions.
sentences.zh: 我们放弃了做一堆数值扩展的计划，一些非常像 NumPy 的数值扩展。

sentences.en: And that would have been very valuable if we had actually done that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的做了那个，那将非常有价值。

sentences.en: And, like, in hindsight, the landscape might have been quite different had we had actually gone through it.
sentences.zh: 而且，事后看来，如果我们真的坚持做下去，前景可能会大不相同。

sentences.en: Why did you abandon it?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么放弃了它？

sentences.en: Nathan ended up going to Google, and Thrust was productized and sort of left our control.
sentences.zh: Nathan 最终去了 Google，Thrust 被产品化了，某种程度上脱离了我们的掌控。

sentences.en: So it became, you know, this product and was sort of maintained by product folks.
sentences.zh: 所以它变成了，你知道的，一个产品，并由产品团队来维护。

sentences.en: So it began as a research project.
sentences.zh: 所以它最初是一个研究项目。

sentences.en: And at some point was decided that we should productize it, which meant finding someone in a product team to sort of own responsibility for it.
sentences.zh: 后来在某个时候决定将其产品化，这意味着要找产品团队的人来负责它。

sentences.en: And at that time, that meant that, you know, the research people that had been working on it to that point would find something else to do.
sentences.zh: 在那时，这意味着之前一直致力于此的研究人员得去找别的事情做了。

sentences.en: And that's essentially what happened.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这么回事。

sentences.en: And so we didn't get Thrust numeric, unfortunately, because of that.
sentences.zh: 很遗憾，因为这个原因，我们没能实现 Thrust 的数值计算功能。

sentences.en: It would have been something like, you know, like expression templates for NumPy-like things, probably.
sentences.zh: 它本来可能会像 NumPy 那样的表达式模板之类的东西。

sentences.en: Something like MatX?
sentences.zh: 类似于 MatX？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: You said MatX?
sentences.zh: 你说 MatX？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Something like that, probably.
sentences.zh: 大概就是那样的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我也不确定。

sentences.en: You can probably still find it on my GitHub, though.
sentences.zh: 不过你可能还能在我的 GitHub 上找到它。

sentences.en: What's interesting is that in the example subdirectory of the what is now cccl slash thrust slash examples, but at one point was thrust slash examples,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在现在叫 cccl/thrust/examples，但曾经叫 thrust/examples 的子目录里，

sentences.en: there are several examples that are basically like array library examples.
sentences.zh: 有几个例子基本上就是数组库的示例。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if Bryce added this, but we had an episode, I don't know if it was 10, 20, 30 episodes ago, where we talked about summed area tables.
sentences.zh: 我不确定是不是 Bryce 加的，但我们之前有一集，不知道是 10 集、20 集还是 30 集前，讨论过求和面积表（summed area tables）。

sentences.en: There is an example in the Thrust example repository of a summed area table in Thrust, which you would think is pretty hard to make happen in Thrust,
sentences.zh: 在 Thrust 的示例仓库里有一个 Thrust 实现的求和面积表示例，你可能会觉得在 Thrust 里实现这个很难，

sentences.en: which is a rank one array library, basically, single sequence.
sentences.zh: 因为它基本上是一个一维数组库，也就是单一序列。

sentences.en: But the way that they do that is they define a function called transpose, which makes use of a permutation iterator and a gather algorithm.
sentences.zh: 但他们的做法是定义了一个叫 transpose 的函数，利用了置换迭代器（permutation iterator）和 gather 算法。

sentences.en: And it just it just calls transpose twice.
sentences.zh: 然后它只是调用了两次 transpose。

sentences.en: And then it defines a horizontal scan, which is implemented in terms of inclusive scan.
sentences.zh: 接着它定义了一个水平扫描（horizontal scan），这是通过 inclusive scan 实现的。

sentences.en: And so it calls that twice interleaved with a transpose algorithm.
sentences.zh: 所以它调用了两次，中间穿插了 transpose 算法。

sentences.en: Anyways, the point being is that like, technically, you can do this with ThruSt.
sentences.zh: 总之，重点是，从技术上讲，你是可以用 Thrust 实现这个的。

sentences.en: It's just non ergonomic.
sentences.zh: 只是用起来不太顺手。

sentences.en: And I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道。

sentences.en: Did you add this example, Bryce?
sentences.zh: 这个例子是你加的吗，Bryce？

sentences.en: No, although I think it was it was one of the original examples, although I do plan on adding another.
sentences.zh: 不是，虽然我觉得它是最初的示例之一，但我确实打算再加一个。

sentences.en: It was one of the original examples.
sentences.zh: 它确实是最初的示例之一。

sentences.en: It's called summed area table.
sentences.zh: 它叫 summed area table。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's called summed underscore area underscore table dot cu.
sentences.zh: 对，它叫 summed_area_table.cu。

sentences.en: And it makes use of inclusive scan by key, which is the where you can, you know, do your kind of row by row key algorithm.
sentences.zh: 它利用了 inclusive_scan_by_key，也就是你可以进行逐行键值算法的地方。

sentences.en: And then it has a transform iterator, which I believe uses a permutation iterator,
sentences.zh: 然后它有一个转换迭代器（transform iterator），我相信它用了一个置换迭代器，

sentences.en: which gets your kind of by column indices and then does a gather at the end of the day to permute your sequence,
sentences.zh: 它获取了列索引，最后通过 gather 来对序列进行置换，

sentences.en: which is I imagine highly inefficient in the in the in the world of, you know, array libraries, machine learning, deep learning.
sentences.zh: 我想在数组库、机器学习、深度学习的世界里，这应该是效率极低的。

sentences.en: But I was very curious to stumble across that the other day, given that you said that you're co-author of the library, Nathan.
sentences.zh: 但那天偶然发现这个我感到非常好奇，毕竟你说你是这个库的合著者，Nathan。

sentences.en: That looks like Nathan code to me.
sentences.zh: 那看起来像是 Nathan 写的代码。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He was always good at figuring out the way to do it.
sentences.zh: 他总是很擅长找出实现方法。

sentences.en: He was he was he was better than me at figuring out how to make the prefix sum do what you wanted.
sentences.zh: 在搞清楚如何让前缀和实现你想要的功能方面，他比我强。

sentences.en: I've gotten better over time, but.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移我进步了一些，但是。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't I don't want to tease too much, but.
sentences.zh: 噢，我不想剧透太多，但是。

sentences.en: But towards the end of the Jared interview, oh, boy, do I have something I've been working on the past two days that I'm very excited to show you guys in that vein.
sentences.zh: 在 Jared 那期访谈快结束时，天哪，我过去两天一直在做一个东西，我很兴奋能在那个方向上展示给你们看。

sentences.en: Be sure to check these show notes either in your podcast app or at adspthepodcaSt.com for links to anything we mentioned in today's episode,
sentences.zh: 请务必查看播客应用中的节目说明，或访问 adspthepodcast.com 获取今天节目中提到的所有链接，

sentences.en: as well as a link to a GitHub discussion where you can leave thoughts, comments and questions.
sentences.zh: 以及一个 GitHub 讨论链接，你可以在那里留下想法、评论和问题。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢，祝你们有愉快的一天。

sentences.en: Low quality, high quantity.
sentences.zh: 低质量，高产量。

sentences.en: That is the tagline of our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们播客的标语。

sentences.en: It's not the tagline.
sentences.zh: 那不是标语。

sentences.en: Our tagline is chaos with sprinkles of information.
sentences.zh: 我们的标语是：充满混乱与零星信息的播客。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoyed and have a great day.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢，祝你们有愉快的一天。
